newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds ended a positive day around 16 basis points firmer on Tuesday, bolstered by good offshore demand after the market initially corrected following a year-low of around 14.45 percent last week.
"There was quite a bit of offshore interest, driving the market stronger," a bond trader said, adding however that he felt the broader correction phase was not yet over.
"It looks like a bit of consolidation in the first phase of the correction and the second phase could swing in soon," he added.
At 1420 GMT government's benchmark R150 bond was at 14.905 percent from 15.05 percent late on Monday.
Bond dealers said the market had followed the currency stronger which gained just under three cents on healthy offshore and local dollar sales.
"Bonds followed the rand which looked pretty good today," one said.
But on the whole it was unclear what had prompted offshore demand after foreigners turned sellers of local bonds on Monday.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners sold a net 323.67 million rands worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 207.26 million on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 6.42 billion rand on Monday from 11.73 billion rand on Friday.
The rand ended just under three cents firmer on the dollar after substantial offshore and local dollar sales sparked by technical factors and expectations of a positive reserves number on Friday.
Generally upbeat comments by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals in an interview with Reuters were also seen behind the gains.
At 1420 GMT the currency was at 4.4420/4470 on the dollar from 4.4700/4730 overnight.

Stals said he believed the rand would hold relatively stable in 1997 after its sharp depreciation last year and that the South African economy could grow by close to three percent in 1997 -- little changed from the 3.1 percent recorded in 1997.
He also expected the central bank's oversold forward foreign exchange book to decline sharply in 1997.
Explaining the technical picture, one senior forex trader said: "After the rand failed to break 4.48 on the upside it tried the bottomside."
Another felt there was room for more strength on Wednesday but that the unit's gains would be capped at the 4.40 level.
"If we close below 4.4485 today we could see the rand consolidate lower around the 4.4250 level on Wednesday but it looks like it will hold 4.40 ahead of the budget," he said.
Against the crosses the rand was last quoted at 7.1796/1889 on sterling from 7.2390/2483 and at 0.3852/3855 marks from 0.3781/3786 marks.

On the money market, the daily shortage rose by close to two billion rand to back above the 10 billion rand mark. The Reserve bank quoted the shortage at 10.548 billion rand on Monday from 8.736 billion rand on Saturday.
Three-month NCD rates held unchanged between 16.50 and 16.70 percent and the 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
